stories.delivered_paragraph: Apple has reportedly delayed its first smart glasses from an early-2027 target to a June 2027 unveiling, with sales expected by year-end, as it works on privacy protections and how to explain them. Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reports Apple plans to stress on-device processing, no facial recognition and no use of customer recordings for AI training. The approach would distinguish Apple from criticism of camera-equipped Meta glasses and test whether privacy can be a competitive feature.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A small but growing group of Democrats, including Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed and California Rep. Ro Khanna, is adopting “America First” language to oppose overseas wars and argue for spending at home. Their effort comes as President Donald Trump’s Iran war alongside Israel has divided the right and loosened his hold on the slogan. The reframing could make foreign-policy restraint a more visible fault line in the 2028 Democratic contest.

stories.delivered_paragraph: A Democratic National Committee panel voted Friday to start the 2028 presidential primary in South Carolina, angering progressives who say the choice favors the party establishment. Bernie Sanders lost South Carolina decisively in both 2016 and 2020, while he won Nevada’s 2020 caucuses; Nevada lost out for the opening slot. The calendar dispute adds to Democratic tensions over 2026 primaries, where party leaders have often backed more centrist candidates over insurgent left-wing challengers.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Israeli settlers set fire to two mosques and attacked cars and agricultural land in West Bank villages overnight, Palestinian officials said, while the Israeli military said troops were sent to Qusra and police would investigate. The attacks followed a clash near Tal two days earlier that killed four Palestinians and two Israelis, with each side blaming the other. The incidents deepen an already volatile cycle of settler and Palestinian violence in the occupied territory.

stories.delivered_paragraph: British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged continued support for Ukraine before hosting President Volodymyr Zelensky on Monday, his first international visitor since taking office a week ago. Burnham will announce that Britain is sharing intellectual property for its tablet-sized “Stone Cloak” electronic-warfare jammer so Ukraine can manufacture it at scale; the UK has already supplied thousands. The technology is intended to help Ukrainian drones evade detection, expanding Kyiv’s ability to sustain its defense against Russia.

stories.delivered_paragraph: MLB contenders are weighing deadline upgrades before the Aug. 3, 6 p.m. ET trade cutoff, with Detroit Tigers ace Tarik Skubal and Boston Red Sox closer Aroldis Chapman among the closely watched names. Detroit’s recent surge has made a Skubal deal less certain, while Boston’s improved position could similarly keep Chapman in place. The next week will determine whether clubs such as the Dodgers, Yankees and Phillies pay heavily for October help or stand pat.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Charli xcx released a digital deluxe version of “Music, Fashion, Film” on iTunes, making three previously physical-only B-sides available to buy online for the first time. The $4.99 edition adds “I Keep On Thinking Bout You Every Single Day and Night,” “Playboy Bunny” and “If You Take the Music Then What Has She Got?” to the album’s original 11 tracks, plus videos. The move reverses her earlier expectation that the songs would not reach streaming or digital platforms.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Tadej Pogačar won the Tour de France for a record-tying fifth time, finishing 6 minutes and 26 seconds ahead after taking the yellow jersey on stage six and holding it through the final 15 stages. The 27-year-old Slovenian joins Eddy Merckx, Miguel Indurain, Bernard Hinault and Jacques Anquetil as five-time winners. His commanding margin, established before rival Jonas Vingegaard’s stage-15 collarbone injury, puts Pogačar in position to pursue the outright record.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Verge argues that John De Hart’s “Champagne and Bullets,” also released as “GetEven” and “Road to Revenge,” deserves a place alongside cult “so-bad-they’re-good” films such as “The Room” and “Troll 2.” De Hart wrote, directed and stars in the low-budget action movie, including an awkward musical performance called “Shimmy Slide.” The review frames the film’s mismatched ambition, stilted performances and baffling scenes as the appeal for viewers seeking outsider-cinema curiosities.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige said director Ryan Coogler chose David Jonsson to lead “Black Panther 3” after a secret meeting roughly six months ago, before the studio had begun a formal casting search. Feige said Coogler, then working on “Sinners,” called to say Jonsson was “the next Black Panther” after meeting him privately. The account confirms the role’s intended direction and ties the franchise’s next installment closely to Coogler’s judgment.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Amazon, Meta, Microsoft and Apple will report results in a crowded week for corporate earnings, while the Federal Reserve’s July policy meeting gives investors another major market test. Boeing reports Tuesday after its shares were pressured by renewed Middle East tensions and higher oil prices, which can weigh on aerospace companies. The combination of Big Tech results, rate policy and oil-driven geopolitical risk could set the near-term direction for stocks.

stories.delivered_paragraph: U.S. stock-index futures rose and oil prices fell Sunday after the United States and Iran paused attacks, easing traders’ immediate concerns about a broader conflict and energy disruption. Markets now turn to the Federal Reserve’s meeting and earnings reports from major technology companies. The relief rally remains tied to whether the pause in fighting holds, because renewed hostilities could quickly push oil higher and unsettle equities again.
